open_questions: No open_questions; rejection is due to non-reproducible depth and secondary-like brightening, not an unmeasured ambiguity.
dossier.public_summary: The claimed 1.4 Earth-radius dip appears only as very deep transits in early sectors (620 ppm, 761 ppm) and two huge outliers (2161 ppm, 1315 ppm), then vanishes to no detection in later sectors, meaning it does not repeat at 14.5 days. A second brightness dip near 0.6 orbital phase and the star’s catalogue binarity flags point to an eclipsing binary blended in TESS’s aperture rather than a planet transiting the target.

reasons.why: Depths not steady even within SPOC 2-min: 620±73 ppm (sec 7), 306±87 (sec 8), 761±68 (sec34), 76±46 (sec35) with p_constant 1.6393659154691014e-18. A calibration difference would be differs_by_source, which it is not.

Signal is dominated by two historic events: 2228.987 2161 ppm (14.1 sigma) and 1491.716 1315 ppm (13.4 sigma), while later sectors 61 and 88 are non-detections (-1±53, 31±81 ppm). The later period, sector 61 (t14 4.199 h, v_sigma -2.39, duration ratio 0.8273 fit_b 0.08178 fit_k 0.01656) is not reproduced.

Brightening with snr ~5.5 matches secondary depth, with secondary_over_bump 0.9639 indicating a second dip of similar significance. ruwe 2.491 non_single_star 1 ipd_harmonic 0.007063 excess_noise_sig 132.9 support a blended/background EB interpretation; secondary is real by snr 5 or more threshold.

reasons.why: Crowded low-contrast field has plausible neighbours close enough to create the 294.2 ppm dip with <25% eclipses, and centroid cannot rule them out, so a neighbour EB that is bright in the early aperture and invisible later remains viable.
